'''David Herbert Munro''' (born April 29, 1955) is a [[physicist]] at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] (LLNL) who created the [[programming language]] [[Yorick programming language|Yorick]] as well as the scientific [[graphics library]] [[Gist (Computing)|Gist]].

Munro earned his [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] at [[Caltech]] (1976) and [[PhD]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1980). He joined LLNL in 1980 and has primarily focused his research on [[laser fusion]].

He received the Excellence in Plasma Physics award of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1995 and was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2001 "For his seminal contributions to the design of laser-driven Rayleigh-Taylor experiments, and to the analysis and design of shock-timing experiments for cryogenic inertial confinement fusion targets".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2001&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate=20 September 2020}}</ref>
